date_note: Date of TeamSpirit's own notice; the data retrieval was confirmed on 27 Oct. ScanNetSecurity reported it on 20 Nov.
title: TeamSpirit: 28,824 personal records leaked after intrusion into software development server
summary: TeamSpirit said a third party logged into its software development server and used credentials stored there to retrieve data from its cloud environment, confirmed on 27 October. As far as confirmed so far, 28,824 personal records (duplicates excluded) leaked, 35 of them sensitive personal information. The company says it was not an unknown vulnerability but configuration and information-management deficiencies on the server. It says credit card and bank account data were not leaked.
plain: TeamSpirit says an attacker got into a development server and pulled data from its cloud, as far as confirmed so far 28,824 personal records.
exec: A workforce-software vendor says 28,824 personal records leaked, as far as confirmed so far, through weak configuration of a development server.
action: TeamSpirit customers should read the company's notice, watch for phishing using the contact details involved, and decide on reporting as the notice advises.

sources.name: TeamSpirit notice, 6 Nov 2026 (apology and notice on information leak from unauthorized access)

validation.note: The company's own notice (6 Nov, updated 9 Nov) and ScanNetSecurity (20 Nov) agree on the figures, dates and cause statement.

review.note: Compared 28,824 (duplicates excluded, as far as confirmed), 35 sensitive, 27 Oct, 6 Nov date, cause statement and no card/bank leak against TeamSpirit notice and ScanNetSecurity
